notes: v2 is a typed port of Go 1.27's package on top of jsontext. Go finds conversions with reflect; here a type implements MarshalTo or UnmarshalFrom (the standard types do, and rust_stdlib_derive::{MarshalTo, UnmarshalFrom} derive them for structs from the #[json(...)] attributes: Go struct tags plus omitempty, omitzero, string, case_ignore, case_strict, inline, unknown (Go's embed option on a map or Value) and format). Error text, byte offsets, JSON Pointers, partial results after errors, merging into existing values and every option are checked against Go by tools/jsonv2_check.py. Rust shapes: an empty Vec or map is both Go's nil and empty (omitzero, FormatNil*AsNull), Go's any is v2::Any, []byte is json::Bytes, pointers are Option, the format tag option is rejected as in Go unless experimental_support_format_tag is set, time.Time and time.Duration use Go's time arshalers (RFC 3339 by default, the format tag layouts and units with experimental_support_format_tag), and the v1 compatibility options (including FormatDurationAsNano and ParseTimeWithLooseRFC3339) are not supported.

ErrUnknownName.note: an Error variant; compare with Error::is

FormatNilMapAsNull.note: Rust has no nil map: an empty map stands for both nil and empty, so the option writes every empty map as null

FormatNilSliceAsNull.note: Rust has no nil slice: an empty Vec stands for both nil and empty, so the option writes every empty Vec as null (the arrays of a decoded Any are never nil)

GetOption.note: the setter is passed as a typed function pointer (for example `deterministic as fn(bool) -> Options`) selecting the OptionSetter impl

Marshal.note: the value is any type implementing MarshalTo (derive it with rust_stdlib_derive::MarshalTo); only the error is returned when marshaling fails, not the partial output; the v1 compatibility options (a json.Options of the v1 package) are not supported

MarshalEncode.note: the value is any type implementing MarshalTo; options are a slice

MarshalFunc.note: T is the exact type of the values the function applies to; Go also accepts interface and pointer types, which dispatch on assignability

MarshalToFunc.note: T is the exact type of the values the function applies to; Go also accepts interface and pointer types

MarshalWrite.note: the value is any type implementing MarshalTo

Marshaler.note: a type returns it from MarshalTo::as_marshaler

MarshalerTo.note: a type returns it from MarshalTo::as_marshaler_to

Options.note: the same set-of-settings type as jsontext::Options

SemanticError.Error.note: the Display text is Go's Error() string, with "cannot" always chosen over "unable to"; a JSON value with invalid UTF-8 shows U+FFFD for each bad byte

SemanticError.GoType.note: a TypeInfo describing the Go type (its reflect.Type.String() text and kind) rather than a reflect.Type

Unmarshal.note: the destination is a &mut T for a type implementing UnmarshalFrom (derive it with rust_stdlib_derive::UnmarshalFrom), updated in place like Go's pointer target; a nil pointer argument cannot occur; the v1 compatibility options are not supported

UnmarshalDecode.note: the destination is a &mut T for a type implementing UnmarshalFrom; options are a slice

UnmarshalFromFunc.note: T is the exact type of the values the function fills in, passed as &mut T; Go's parameter is a pointer or interface type

UnmarshalFunc.note: T is the exact type of the values the function fills in, passed as &mut T; Go's parameter is a pointer or interface type

UnmarshalRead.note: the destination is a &mut T for a type implementing UnmarshalFrom

Unmarshaler.note: a type returns it from UnmarshalFrom::as_unmarshaler

UnmarshalerFrom.note: a type returns it from UnmarshalFrom::as_unmarshaler_from
